summary: The bill amends federal criminal law to make it a felony, punishable by up to 10 years in prison, for anyone to knowingly misrepresent the source or nature of DNA used in assisted reproductive technology or insemination procedures when the conduct involves interstate commerce, and extends the statute of limitations for such offenses.

scores.thoughts: The bill contains no provisions related to federal spending, appropriations, or budgets. It focuses solely on creating a new criminal offense.
No tax-related language, rates, credits, or revenue measures appear in the bill.

While the bill addresses assisted reproductive technology (a medical procedure), it does so exclusively through criminal penalties for fraud rather than altering coverage, access, funding, or the public/private structure of healthcare delivery.
The bill has no connection to firearms, gun regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
No immigration, border, or visa provisions are present.
The legislation concerns misrepresentation of DNA in fertility treatments but does not address abortion access, restrictions, or related procedures.
No military, defense, or national security spending or policy elements exist.
The bill contains nothing related to environmental regulations, climate policy, or natural resources.
No welfare, entitlement, or social assistance programs are mentioned or altered.
The bill has no bearing on schools, education funding, or school choice.
No drug enforcement, decriminalization, or controlled-substance provisions are included.

The bill creates a new federal felony (up to 10 years imprisonment) for misrepresenting DNA in assisted reproductive technology, extends the statute of limitations when DNA testing identifies the offender, and adds the offense to the RICO predicate list. This directly expands criminal liability and federal prosecutorial tools.
No trade, tariff, or globalization measures are present.
The bill does not address deficits, debt reduction, or fiscal policy.
No provisions touch on LGBTQ legal protections or related civil rights.
Foreign aid is not mentioned.
The bill contains no election, voting access, or election-integrity provisions.
No data-privacy, technology regulation, or surveillance rules are involved.
Labor, union, or employment-law matters are absent.
The bill does not engage with religious exemptions or anti-discrimination balances.
